title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 54-56). P_· is the k-linear additive category of finite (bounded) complexes of finite free k-modules. Σ is the class of degreewise split short exact sequences, with respect to which 'Σ-exact', 'Σ-épi', 'Σ-ker' and 'Σ-sex' (Σ-semi-exact, i.e. left exact) are meant. Two families of objects generate everything:
- the disks C^i_· (h --id--> h in two adjacent degrees, so contractible);
- the spheres Ψ^i_· (h in a single degree).
They are related by Σ-exact sequences 0 → Ψ^i → C^i → Ψ^{i+1} → 0, and the maps C^i → C^{i+1} assemble into a cochain complex C^· in P_·.

The theorem being proved is a universal property of P_·. For a suitable target B (with a good class Σ of exact sequences, in which morphisms admit Σ-kernels), evaluation at the 'universal complex' gives an equivalence
ρ: Hom_{k,Σ-sex}(P_·, B) → B^· (cochain complexes in B), F ↦ F(C^·).
The quasi-inverse is σ(C^·)(L_·) = Hom^·_k(L^·, C^·), the Z^0 of the internal Hom complex (L^· the dual complex).

Proof (finished at the top of this page):
1. The unit F → σρF is an isomorphism on disks and spheres, using F(Ψ^i) = F(Ker(C^i → C^{i+1})) = Z^i(F(C^·)) by left exactness.
2. By induction on the length [p,q] of L_·, write L_· as the fibre product of its truncation L'_· and (C^p)^r over (Ψ^{p+1})^r. Equivalently, L_· is the kernel of a Σ-epi (C^p)^r × L'_· → (Ψ^{p+1})^r.
3. Left exactness of F then propagates the isomorphism to all of P_·.

NB. If B is not assumed to have the needed Σ-kernels, the argument only shows that ρ is fully faithful ('pl. fid.'). Its adjoint σ is then valued in Σ-sex functors to an ind-completion B^, and one still has σρ ≃ id, i.e. F(L_·) ≃ Hom^·(L^·, F(C^·)) for every Σ-sex F.

Re NB. Under F ↔ C^· = F(C^·), F is fully Σ-exact iff C^· is a Σ-resolution, i.e. Σ-acyclic.

Example begun. Take B = Ab_k and F = Hom_{Ab_{k·}}(A_·, −) for a complex A_·. This F is Σ-left exact, and in fact left exact. The next page identifies the corresponding complex via the duality Hom(A_·, L_·) ≅ Hom(L^∨, A^∨).

In modern terms: the category of bounded finite free complexes, with its degreewise-split exact structure, is the free 'left exact k-linear' category on a cochain complex. Equivalently, chain complexes in B are the left exact functors out of it. This is a 1-categorical, exact-category ancestor of 'Perf_k is the free stable k-linear idempotent-complete ∞-category on one object'. It presumably serves the dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and of multiplicative structures, by reducing functors on perfect complexes to complexes.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The NB is correctly hedged: without kernels in B, σ must land in an ind-completion B^, and one only gets full faithfulness.
Gaps: the precise hypotheses on (B, Σ) ('bonne classe Σ des suites exactes') are left implicit. The duality L ↦ L^· used in σ (Hom from the dual complex) is not spelled out on this page.

ideas.what: Equivalence between Σ-left-exact k-linear functors on bounded finite free complexes and cochain complexes in B, given by evaluation at the universal complex of disks C^·, with inverse L ↦ Z^0 Hom^·(L^∨, C^·)
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the exact (Frobenius) category of complexes, Ch(B) ≃ Lex(Ch^b(proj k), B); 1-categorical analogue of the universal property of Perf_k among stable ∞-categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. Related: Gabriel–Roiter and Keller (exact/Frobenius structure on complexes, ~1990); Lurie (stable universal property of Sp^ω / Perf, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; Les Dérivateurs treats universal properties of derivators, not this exact-category statement

ideas.what: Dévissage of a finite complex as an iterated fibre product of disks and spheres (L = L' ×_{Ψ^{p+1 r}} (C^p)^r), giving induction on length
ideas.modern_name: Cell/skeletal filtration of complexes by disks D^n and spheres S^n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (model structure on Ch, Hovey etc.)

ideas.what: Criterion: F is Σ-exact iff the associated complex F(C^·) is Σ-acyclic
ideas.modern_name: Exact functors from complexes correspond to acyclic complexes (cf. Fun^ex(Perf, C) and contractible/acyclic objects)

missed.claim: A clean universal property: k-linear Σ-left-exact functors from bounded finite free complexes (degreewise split exact structure) to B are equivalent to cochain complexes in B, via F ↦ F(C^·). This comes with a fully faithful version when B lacks kernels, and an exactness criterion (F exact ⇔ F(C^·) acyclic). It is an early 1-categorical precursor of 'Perf_k is free on one object' universal properties.
missed.quote: Hom_{k,Σ-sex}(P_·,B) ≈→ B^· ... F est Σ-exact ssi C^· est une Σ-résolution
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Likely known in folklore, but rarely stated explicitly in this exact-category form. It shows Grothendieck around 1975 already characterising complex categories by universal properties, ahead of derivator and ∞-categorical formulations.

deep.surprise_reason: A neat, complete universal-property statement for categories of complexes, proved by disk/sphere dévissage. It is conceptually anticipatory of later stable universal properties, but specialists would regard the statement itself as folklore-level.
transcription_corrections: 'des sous[?] exactes' is likely 'des suites exactes' (bonne classe Σ de suites exactes).
'F(𝕃_·)' / 'F(𝕃^·)' should be F(ℂ^·), the complex of disks, whose image is denoted C^·.
'λ_· ∈ Ab_{k_·}' is probably 'A_· ∈ Ab_{k·}' (complexes of k-modules), consistent with the next page's A_·.
In the NB, read roughly: 'si on ne suppose pas que B admette des Σ-noyaux, mais seulement que les morphismes de B^· admettent un noyau (dans B^)...'
